title: Trajectory-controlled model swap with checkpointed failsafe and cohort-aware rewind
author: Priya Narang
description:
Background and motivation: Large model swaps during rollouts (A/B and cohort-based canaries) can leave partial state that makes automatic rollback brittle — KV cache divergence, in-flight prefixes, and cohort-level traffic splits lead to hard-to-reproduce failures. This PR introduces the concept of a 'trajectory' for a model swap: a tracked, checkpointed progression of cohorts through deterministic safe points with a compact snapshot format that enables fast, cohort-targeted rewind and deterministic replay for post-failure diagnostics.

High level changes: Adds a TrajectoryCoordinator responsible for (1) defining swap safe-points, (2) checkpointing per-cohort serving state (KV cache pointers, model version binding, routing tokens), (3) exposing a rewind API that can move a single cohort or full rollout back to a prior checkpoint, and (4) providing a Replayer CLI to deterministically replay traffic for debugging and regression replay. Checkpointing is incremental and asynchronous to avoid impacting tail latency; checkpoints are stored in the checkpoint store with deduplication by prefix hash.

Why this is different: prior PRs focused on atomic swap or traffic splitting alone. This change encodes lifecycle metadata as a first-class object (Trajectory) so rollouts can be advanced, paused, or rewound to known-good checkpoints — enabling safe partial rollbacks, differential replay for SLO regression hunting, and targeted remediation without global rollbacks.

Compatibility & migration: Default behavior is opt-in via rollout policy field trajectory_enabled: true. Existing rollout controllers remain unchanged unless the new field is set. Checkpoint store uses existing blob storage backend (S3/GCS) with a small new index table in the serving metadata DB; migration is additive and guarded by a feature flag.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for coordinator state machine and checkpoint serializer; integration tests that run a model swap across 3 cohorts and execute a cohort rewind; an e2e scenario that verifies KV cache checkpoint/replay preserves model outputs across a rewind. Perf microbenchmarks show <1% p99 tail regression when checkpointing is enabled with default sampling policy.

Operational notes: Adds trajectory.* metrics (trajectory_progress, checkpoint_duration_seconds, rewind_duration_seconds, replay_consistency_rate). New runbook doc at docs/runbooks/trajectory-rewind.md describing when to trigger targeted rewinds and how to interpret replayer traces.

Checklist: 
- [x] Coordinator implementation with safe-point semantics
- [x] Checkpoint store + serializer (dedup by prefix)
- [x] Replayer CLI for deterministic replay
- [x] Integration + e2e tests
- [x] Docs + runbook
- [x] Feature-flag gating and migration guide

Related work: builds on ENG-4821 (cohort-aware traffic controller) and ENG-4833 (kv-cache snapshotting). Supports on-call workflows in SUP-2109.

Notes for reviewers: focus on snapshot size bounds, privacy/encryption (checkpoints contain only routing metadata and KV pointers; cached keys are not materialized unless replay is requested and executed inside a secured job with KMS unseal), and the retention policy recommended in the runbook (default 7 days, can be configured per-tenant).

review_comments: Alexei Morozov (2025-01-20): Can you add a retention policy default and make it tenant-configurable? Also, please clarify whether checkpoints contain any model weights or secrets.

Priya Narang (2025-01-21): Checkpoints only reference KV prefixes and routing bindings; they do not materialize weights or secrets. Added retention config and docs entry explaining tenant override. See commit fa3c8e5 for change.
Maya Chen (2025-01-22): The async checkpoint flush path looked racy under heavy batch load — can we add a retry with backoff and a circuit-breaker to avoid head-of-line blocking?
Priya Narang (2025-01-23): Implemented retry+exponential backoff and a soft circuit-breaker for checkpointing; added unit tests that inject transient store failures.
Diego Alvarez (2025-01-27): Integration test failed in CI on first run due to a timing assumption in the replay harness (sleep windows). Please make tests robust or use event hooks instead.
Priya Narang (2025-01-28): Reworked integration test to rely on event hooks from the test harness rather than fixed sleeps; re-ran the integration suite locally and in CI.
release_notes: Adds optional trajectory-controlled model swap feature: checkpointed safe-points, cohort-targeted rewind, and a deterministic replayer for debugging. Opt-in via rollout policy (trajectory_enabled). Backwards compatible and feature-flag gated.
notes_for_oncall: If a trajectory rewind is executed, the serving logs include trajectory.id and checkpoint.id tags. Use cmd/replayer to run deterministic replay in a secure worker; follow docs/runbooks/trajectory-rewind.md for steps. If checkpoint store is unreachable, the coordinator will pause new trajectory advances and emit trajectory.checkpoint_unavailable metrics.
migration_steps: 1) Enable feature flag in control plane; 2) run migrations/20250112_add_checkpoint_index.sql against metadata DB; 3) configure checkpoint store (S3/GCS) path and KMS policy; 4) roll out coordinator on a small pilot tenant and validate metrics; 5) gradually enable per-rollout via trajectory_enabled=true.
